1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable spacing and an airy card layout, though the monospace log lines wrap awkwardly mid-word ("enrolmen t").

2.why: Instructions are short, sentence-case lines with no italics, no all-caps text (only acronyms like MFA/OTP and the [SIMULATION] log tags), and no dense paragraphs.

3.why: All 13 screenshots are desktop-width; the narrow single-column card would likely adapt to small screens, but readability at a mobile size is never actually demonstrated.

4.why: Each step carries one short, plain instruction (e.g., "Generate backup codes and store them safely"), though "manual Base32 secret" is technical jargon.

5.why: The sign-in fields are prefilled, but the one input the user must actually type — the authenticator code at step 5 — is empty with no placeholder or example of the expected six-digit format.

6.why: Every required instruction is a single short line; only the optional Logs panel holds longer text, though step 5 does direct the user to extract the code from that dense log block.

7.why: The 32-character secret and the recovery codes are rendered as selectable monospace text, but no copy button or copy-all affordance appears on any screen.

8.why: No QR code or otpauth:// link is offered anywhere; step 3 explicitly instructs "Use this manual Base32 secret in an authenticator app."

9.why: Only standard prefilled text inputs are shown, with no evidence (autocomplete hints, password-manager prompts) confirming or denying autofill and password-manager support.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and a single prominent blue primary button, though the large black Logs panel competes for visual attention.

11.why: Every step centres on one main action (Sign in securely, Confirm identity, Create authenticator secret, etc.), with secondary actions like Log out and Regenerate codes visually de-emphasised.

12.why: What comes next is always clear from the next screen's heading, but what happened is confirmed only via technical "[SIMULATION]..." log lines; only the final "MFA is active" screen states the outcome in plain language.

13.why: Codes can be re-viewed ("View recovery codes") and re-requested ("Regenerate codes") without visible penalty, but no hide control and no retry-after-error flow are shown.

14.why: No error message appears in any of the 13 screenshots, so whether errors explain the problem and fix without blame cannot be confirmed.

15.why: No countdowns, timers, or session-expiry warnings appear on any screen, although real TOTP codes inherently rotate every 30 seconds (the test code 627186 is static here).
